NutriCorp Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCorp Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a landline or the button provided if joining via webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCorp Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Growth Officer; and Pat Nguyen, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan.

Mike Harlan (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: key achievements and challenges in the quarter; impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue; impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions; EPS guidance and key assumptions; organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year; overall company performance highlights; and volume and price/mix analysis.

These areas highlight our operational resilience and strategic execution in beverages, snacks, and nutritionals. For instance, we saw robust top-line momentum from premium products like our PureThirst hydration line and VitaCrunch protein bars, alongside disciplined cost management. Challenges like commodity inflation and FX volatility were notable, but our hedging and pricing power kept us ahead. Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $2.82 billion, representing a 4.2% increase year-over-year on a reported basis, or a robust 7.0% on a constant-currency and organic basis excluding FX and acquisitions. Gross margin expanded to 38.4%, up 240 basis points, despite commodity pressures. Operating income was $550 million, and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $0.92, up 14% from last year. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $800 million in cash and marketable securities, net debt to EBITDA at 2.1x. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and $1 billion in share repurchases this year.

To give you deeper context on the seven areas Mike outlined, let me walk through our key achievements and challenges first. Good morning again, everyone—I'm thrilled with how we shaped our performance this quarter in this dynamic Food & Beverage landscape. Our reported net revenues hit $2.82 billion, up 7.5% year-over-year, or 5.2% organically excluding FX and acquisitions. Adjusted EBITDA landed at $540 million, delivering a 19.1% margin, up 110 basis points.

On achievements, we drove strong top-line momentum across core segments—beverages, snacks, and nutritionals—via volume growth and targeted pricing amid inflation. Organic volume rose 3.8%, beating the industry average of 1.2% per NielsenIQ, thanks to premiumization. In beverages, PureThirst electrolyte-enhanced waters, similar to Gatorade's natural flavor evolutions, posted 12% volume growth, gaining 1.2 share points in U.S. functional beverages through distribution into 5,000 more doors at Walmart and Kroger, plus 25% e-commerce surge on our D2C site and Amazon.

Snacks shone with VitaCrunch plant-based protein bars, akin to Kind and RXBAR, up 15% to $320 million in revenue. We launched into 10 new international markets like Southeast Asia, boosting APAC revenues 18% to $180 million—now 14% of total sales—and tapping health snacking trends. Operationally, our Supply Chain Resilience 2.0 initiative rationalized 15% of low-velocity SKUs, optimized yields in co-packers, and deployed AI demand forecasting with SAP IBP, cutting inventory 8% to $450 million while hitting 98% service levels. Sustainability advanced too: 85% Rainforest Alliance-certified cocoa for chocolate snacks beat Nestlé benchmarks, securing premium space at Whole Foods. On M&A, our $150 million BioFuel Beverages buyout added $20 million in Q3 revenue from kombucha and adaptogen shots in the $12 billion functional drinks market growing 9% CAGR per Euromonitor, with integration ahead of plan at 25% EBITDA margins.

Challenges included commodity inflation dragging inputs 6%, with sugar up 22%, cocoa 45% from West African shortages like Hershey's issues, and dairy 15%. We offset via 70% hedging for 2024 and 4% price hikes with no volume loss. EMEA revenues were flat at $220 million, down 2% organically from UK/Germany recessions hitting ready-to-drink coffees like at Keurig Dr Pepper, plus 10% euro FX headwind. North America, 65% of portfolio, dipped 2% in mass carbonated soft drinks as consumers shifted to Aldi private labels, though share held at 4.1% per IRI. Supply disruptions from Red Sea routes added 12 days and 20% freight costs to APAC; Midwest labor shortages cost $8 million, eased by 30% nearshoring to Mexico. Regulatory hits like California sugar labeling cost $12 million in R&D for 20% of snacks, while private labels from Costco Kirkland took 0.5 points in entry nutritionals.

Looking ahead, Q4 eyes 6-8% organic growth and 19.5-20.5% EBITDA via holiday promos, PureThirst Zero launch, and $50 million automation savings. We're pushing app personalization for Gen Z subscriptions, per Mintel.

Shifting to the impact of foreign exchange on revenue, with 58% from outside North America like peers PepsiCo and Coke, FX was a 2.8-point headwind or $79 million drag, making constant-currency growth 7.0%; YTD it's 3.1% or $215 million. The strong USD, DXY at 105.2 up 4.6%, mirrors PepsiCo's 2% and Coke's 3-4% EM hits.

Regionally: Europe (28%) saw euro down 5.2% for $32 million hit; reported growth 1.5%, ex-FX 6.7% from AquaFizz volumes amid EU regs, with Warsaw local production at 65% domestic sourcing. LatAm (15%) took $28 million from Brazil real -8.1% and Mexico peso -4.3%, reported down 2.1% but ex-FX +5.2% on NutriJuice and CrispWave. APAC (12%) $14 million drag from AUD/INR/CNY weakness; India up 12% ex-FX on AquaFizz, China muted. North America (42%) FX-neutral at +6.8%.

Q3's 2.8% headwind flips last year's 1.2% tailwind; Q4 projects 2.0-2.5%. Mitigations: 72% 2024 revenue hedged (Q3 gains $22 million), 48% local COGS, 85% FX pass-through pricing, ASEAN tilt, and SAP AI modeling post-$500M equity issuance.

Next, input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions. COGS rose 11.8%, with wheat +22% from Ukraine issues like at Mondelez/General Mills, corn +18% on droughts, dairy +14% from avian flu, palm oil +25% on Indonesia curbs, aluminum +16%. Freight 150% over 2019, energy +28% in Europe. This compressed gross margins 320 bps to 35.0%-ish before offsets.

Disruptions stretched cocoa leads to 16 weeks from Red Sea/West Africa; 15-20% APAC stockouts like Unilever tea; U.S. warehouse delays inflated working capital $45 million, turns to 6.2x. North America passed 70% costs on premiums; Europe squeezed by Green Deal; APAC localized palm oil; LatAm currency offsets.

Responses: 75% hedged wheat/corn saving $28 million, 30% Colombian palm oil, Midwest corn milling for 200 bps savings, SAP IBP at 92% accuracy cutting stock 18%, digital twins for 3% yields, blockchain for cocoa. Pricing 8-10% on 65% portfolio held velocity. FY24 COGS to 6-8%, margins to 36.5%.

On EPS guidance and key assumptions for FY2024, we're at $5.85 to $6.05 adjusted diluted, 11-16% growth over $5.28, no major M&A beyond $450M GreenLeaf Bites, no tariffs. Organic revenue 5-7%, 60% pricing (H1 4.2%, Q4 ~2%), 40% volume/mix from functionals +12% like VitaSpark, 35% health SKUs. NA 6-8%, EMEA 3-5%, APAC 7-9%, LatAm 4-6%. Gross margins 42.5-43.0% (+150-200 bps) via $250-300M productivity, 4-6% input inflation (70% hedged). Op margins 20.0-20.5%, A&P 11-12%, SG&A flat, $1.2B capex. Tax 22-23%, shares 1.05B, interest $180M, FCF 95%+ for $2.5-2.8B dividends/$1.5B buybacks. Risks: palm shortages, private labels, GLP-1; upsides: China volumes.

For organic sales growth guidance, FY2024 hit 6.2% vs 4-6%, now Q1 FY2025 5-7% (volumes 2.5-3.5%, pricing 1.5-2.0%), full FY2025 6-8% to $28.5-29.2B. Drivers: 12 Q1 NPDs like QuenchCore zero-sugar, 18% SKU delist boosting ACV; e-comm 22%, c-stores. NA 6-8%, EMEA 3-5%, APAC/LatAm 8-10%. FY2025: $450M capex Mexico plant, AI forecasting, RegenAg emissions -18%, vs GLP-1 via functional bites.

Overall performance highlights: Revenues $2.82B up 9% reported/7% organic—eighth straight quarter—3% volume, 4% pricing. Beverages (45%) +11% on Quench Energy/VitaGlow +25%; snacks +6% despite cocoa +40%. Op income $2.9B wait no—scaled: adjusted op income robust 22.7% margin +180 bps via $450M ERP/AI savings, turns 8.2x. EPS $0.92 +14%, FCF $800M+ 110% conversion. Nutrition +15% post-CleanEats, 25% margins. NA +10% share +80 bps, e-comm 18%; APAC +12% China RTD; LatAm +8%; Europe +4%. Raised FY organic to 6-7%, EPS $6.10-6.20; divested non-core, 20 NPDs, 65% RSPO palm.

Finally, volume and price/mix: Organic revenue +7.2%, volumes -0.5% (better than Q2 -1.2%), price/mix +7.7% (4.2% pricing, 3.5% mix). Beverages -1.1% total (+4.2% healthies like AquaZest/VitaBoost vs CSD -2.3%); snacks flat (+6.7% protein FlexBars). NA -1.2% (+3.4% c-stores), EMEA flat, APAC +1.8%, LatAm -2.4%/+1.1% Brazil. Pricing waves 8-10% offset +7% COGS; mix +150 bps premiums (functionals +12% ASP). Premium First $250M RGM AI, sustainability +15% premium. Q4 6-8%, flat volumes.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 6-8% organic growth and adjusted EPS $5.85-6.05.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Chris Murphy with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Chris Murphy (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Mike Harlan (CEO):
Thanks, Chris. Inflation remains a top headwind, with COGS up 11.8% from wheat +22%, corn +18%, dairy +14%, palm +25%, and packaging/energy spikes. Combined with disruptions like cocoa lead times to 16 weeks and Red Sea freight +20%, it compressed margins 320 bps pre-mitigation. But we hedged 75% of grains saving $28M, diversified palm to Colombia, invested in corn milling for 200 bps savings, and used AI for 92% forecasting accuracy and 3% yield gains. Pricing passed 65-70% through on premiums, holding velocity flat per Circana. Regionally, NA pricing power strong, Europe tougher on regs. FY24 inflation moderates to 6-8%, positioning margins ahead of peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Lisa Wong (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for new products like PureThirst Zero and what is the expected impact?

Jordan Lee (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Lisa. PureThirst Zero is a cornerstone of our Q4 launches, extending our hydration leadership with low-sugar, stevia-sweetened carbonated waters targeting the $15B functional market +12% per IRI. Plans include 12 NPDs in Q1 FY25, building on PureThirst's 12% uplift via 5,000 more doors and e-comm. Expect 1-2 points mix tailwind, 6-8% NA growth, with functionals now 22-35% portfolio driving 11-15% category outperformance like VitaSpark or FlexBars. Sustainability packaging cuts plastic 15%, unlocking EU shelf space and +15% ASP. Overall, innovation adds 20% household penetration, countering private labels and GLP-1 with fiber-enriched bites.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

David Kim (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Pat Nguyen (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Thanks, David. Disruptions persist from Red Sea +12 days/20% freight, cocoa 16-week leads, Midwest labor $8M hit, and port strife delaying pallets 10-14 days, slowing turns to 6.2x. We're nearshoring 30% beverages to Mexico, localizing 48-65% sourcing (e.g., Warsaw, Gujarat plant), and using SAP IBP AI for 92% accuracy/18% stock cuts. Blockchain with IBM cut cocoa disputes 60%; digital twins boosted bottling 3%. SKU rationalization culls 15-18% low-velocity, inventory -8%; RegenAg with 500 suppliers -18% emissions, $50M green financing. Mexico capex covers 25% NA needs; expect normalization via Panama dredging, exiting FY25 turns 7.5x+.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Patel with Bank of America. Please proceed.

Emily Patel (Bank of America):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Chen (CFO):
Emily, our outlook remains strong. Q4 organic 6-8%, EBITDA 19.5-20.5% via promos, automation $50M, PureThirst Zero. FY25 Q1 5-7%, full year 6-8% to $28.5-29.2B, accelerating H2 volumes 4%. Embeds sugar -5%, dairy stable; 200 bps margin expansion to 38-39%. EPS $5.85-6.05 FY24, raised to $6.10-6.20. FX 2-2.5% drag, but 72% hedged; upsides China volumes, disinflation; risks cocoa/El Niño, but 85% covered. FCF funds returns; confident in 12% TSR.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mike Harlan for closing remarks.

Mike Harlan (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriCorp Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
